run1_no_tracks.question: How many people walked through the shopping centre corridor between 9:44 and 9:54 am?

What was recorded (coverage is 09:44:10 to 09:53:39, so up to ~09:53:40, not the full minute to 09:54):

- Caption logs for the same window typically report 4-6 people, occasionally 7-11 when far-background figures are included.

How I got this: checked track tables (no data) then counted persons on 6 frames and cross-checked the 10-sec caption people-counts - medium confidence for occupancy level, low confidence for any total-throughflow number.

How I got this: visual review of 5 frames from phone-68 plus an automatic person count as a second check. Confidence medium - grouping is by visual proximity/direction, and frames are spot-checks, not a full continuous count.

run2_tracks_and_identities.question: How many people stopped to look at shop windows or browse, instead of just walking past?
run2_tracks_and_identities.answer:
On the shopping centre corridor (phone-68), 09:44-09:53 UTC on 2 Nov 2026 (~9.5 min covered):

39 distinct person-identities were seen in total.

- ~12 just walked past: seen for <10 sec ( 7.5, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 1.0, 0.5, 0x4 sec ) - single brief fragment crossing the view.
- ~27 lingered / were in view for >=10 sec, up to ~9 min:
  - 18 customers with 39 sec to ~9.3 min in view
  - 9 staff with ~3.7 min to ~9.4 min in view

That is the best proxy for "stopped to look / browse vs just walking past" from the tracks: short = through-walker, long + small pixel movement = standing at the left-side shop glazing or by the right-side pillar / rail / bin, or going in/out of a shop.

How checked: identity_spans dwell times for phone-68 person + identity_notes role (customer vs staff) + foot-pixel spread per identity (small rx+ry = standing, large rx ~400-600 px = walking the length of the corridor) + visual check of 6 frames across the period showing 5-6 people at once along the left glazing and right pillar. Camera is not calibrated in metres and there is no gaze / shop-door zone, and long identities spanning the whole 9 min suggest some re-identification merging, so treat 18 browsing customers vs 12 quick passers as approximate, not an exact window-gaze count.

run2_tracks_and_identities.question: Did people walk alone or in groups? How many groups did we see?

On the shopping centre corridor (phone-68) on 2 Nov 2026, 09:44-09:53 UTC - about 9.5 min covered:

- 39 person-identities in total, max 7 visible at one instant, typically 1-3.
- Visual check at 09:44:15, 09:47:30, 09:50:00, 09:52:30: 15 person boxes seen, all as solitary walkers in the foreground/mid-ground - no confirmed close pair walking arm-in-arm.
- Captions repeatedly describe "a single person walks... walking alone" and "very quiet corridor" - e.g. 09:51:38-09:51:48 one customer alone, 09:51:26 one person pauses at shopfront then continues alone.

Groups seen: 2-3 small background groups:
- Early 09:44:18-09:44:30: 6 people clustered far down the corridor (foot-x 158-268px) + 1 foreground person alone - likely 1 group of 3-4 plus other singles.
- 09:47:39 caption: "small group of shoppers visible walking away / standing near the far end" behind a single woman in foreground.
- 09:52:35 caption: "small group moving through + two people standing farther down" - 5 people in view.

So: ~ 80-90% singles, plus about 2-3 small groups of 2-4 people in the far background. Low confidence on exact group count because the view is long-distance, low-resolution and far figures overlap.

How I got it: counted identity_spans (39), counted simultaneous track_points per timestamp, looked at 4 marked frames with Glimmer, and searched captions for group/pair/together/alone.
